angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 660,915 km at 178.11 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.6146 +/- 0.0259 mas (same row, RUWE 1.28): 178.11 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.95 +/- 0.02 solar radii from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-352 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract): 660,915 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.98 +/- 0.04 solar masses from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-352 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5791 +/- 81 K from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-352 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-352 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-352.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.474, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
